lines.text: Many learners say: I have a doubt about this word.
Better: I have a question about this word.
To ask for help, say question, not doubt.
Question! I have a question about this word.

data.wrong: I have a doubt about this word.
data.right: I have a question about this word.
data.why: To ask for help, say question, not doubt.

quiz.stem: I have a ___ about this word.

native.tip: En español decimos “tengo una duda”, pero en inglés para pedir ayuda se dice “I have a question.”
native.caption: 🙈 Error común: “I have a doubt about this word.” En inglés “doubt” suena a desconfianza; para preguntar algo se dice “I have a question about this word.” ¡Escucha a Ama y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “question”. Para pedir ayuda se dice “I have a question”, no “I have a doubt”. Escribe una frase tuya con “I have a question” o dila en voz alta: {link}

en.tip: Learners say “tengo una duda”, but in English you say “I have a question.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “I have a doubt about this word.” In English, “doubt” sounds like you do not trust something. Say “I have a question about this word.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
